basis: Heterogeneous umbrella; renal disease predominates in common ciliopathies. Retinal, neurologic and airway damage depend on subtype.
Cobalamin remethylation defect with megaloblastic anemia; developmental impairment and cerebral abnormalities occur in 30-79% or more. Damaging ocular disease is not established as common.
Teratoma arising within the spinal cord.
Neoplasm of the sublingual salivary gland; salivary glands belong to the gastrointestinal axis.
Hypogonadotropic hypogonadism; dental abnormalities and osteopenia each affect 2/5 patients. Hearing impairment affects 1/5; anosmia frequency is unspecified.
Superficial fungal infection directly occupying the skin.
Benign angiomyolipoma arising in the kidney during childhood.
Structural bone disorders; neurologic compression is subtype-dependent and not intrinsic to the entire umbrella.
Inherited myopia is an ocular refractive and growth disorder.
B-lymphoblastic leukemia/lymphoma affects hematopoietic cells; the explicit lymphoma classification supports the immune mechanism axis.
Adenomatoid mesothelial tumor of the peritoneum, assigned to the gastrointestinal axis.
Autoimmune lupus; pericarditis and cytopenias annotated 80-99%. Renal annotations conflict with typically rare nephritis; arthralgia and myalgia alone do not establish tissue damage.
Inherited defective dental enamel maturation; teeth belong to the gastrointestinal axis.
Isolated cblD remethylation defect with homocystinuria and megaloblastic anemia; neurodevelopmental impairment is characteristic and common, approximately over 30%.
Growth restriction and skeletal dysmorphism define this Silver-Russell subtype; clinodactyly affects 30-79%. Neurologic, cardiac and hypoglycemic findings are occasional.
Defining limb and skeletal dysplasia; gingival overgrowth and short lingual frenulum each affect 3/6, retained primary teeth 2/6. Facial and ocular appearance alone adds no axis.
Epilepsy, intellectual disability and speech apraxia define a neurologic syndrome.
Biallelic BEST1-associated disease directly affects the retina.
Severe skeletal dysplasia; pulmonary hypoplasia and structural airway abnormalities commonly impair respiration across types, exceeding approximately 30%.
Infection-related syndromic umbrella; direct damage to particular organs varies across congenital infectious and inflammatory subtypes.
Tumor defined by central nervous system occupation, including primary dural tumors; adjacent bone origin or extension is not universal.
Substance-induced psychiatric perceptual disorder; visual hallucinations do not establish ocular disease or direct neurologic tissue damage.
Inherited acute myeloid leukemia directly affects marrow and blood cells; the connective-tissue ancestor does not establish musculoskeletal disease.
Chronic allergic immune-mediated inflammation directly damages the esophagus.
Noninflammatory degeneration and lysis of arterial media; ischemic injury to supplied organs varies and is not assumed common.
